queer_characters.name: Omar Shanaa
queer_characters.notes: Closeted gay character who struggles with family expectations, comes out, and pursues relationships with Ander and others; his coming-out arc explores cultural and class tensions.

queer_characters.name: Ander Munoz
queer_characters.notes: Gay athlete and principal's son with a leukaemia storyline in Season 3; central to a long-running same-sex relationship.

queer_characters.name: Polo Benavent
queer_characters.notes: Initially closeted, later explores relationships with both a woman (Cayetana) and a man (Valerio), which the text presents as bisexuality.

queer_characters.name: Patrick Blanco
queer_characters.notes: Gay character who develops relationships with Omar, Ander, and eventually Ivan.

queer_characters.name: Ivan Cruz
queer_characters.notes: Gay character with relationships with Patrick and later Joel.

queer_characters.name: Joel Castellano
queer_characters.notes: Gay character, boyfriend to Omar, who later has an affair with Ivan.

queer_characters.name: Nico Fernandez
queer_characters.notes: Transgender character who undergoes gender affirmation surgery and a legal name change within the show.

contributor_notes: Source text describes a Season 6 hate-crime murder of a gay character motivated by homophobia, which supports the bury-your-gays flag, though the specific character killed is not named in the provided text — a maintainer should verify. No queer creators are identified in the source material; audio/subtitle info is limited to the series being Spanish-language. Spicy level 4 reflects the source's note of 'sensual and explicit' gay male sex scenes. The series won a 2019 GLAAD Media Award (Outstanding Scripted Television, Spanish-Language).
